subject.title: fix(agents): preserve operator.write scope for in-process subagent spawns

question: Is successful `sessions_spawn` tool authorization sufficient to let its internal in-process `agent` RPC run as a synthetic operator with `operator.write`, rather than retaining the originating channel or plugin request principal?
rationale: Source inspection proves the synthetic principal is limited to write scope, but repository evidence cannot determine whether tool authorization or caller identity is the intended permanent security boundary.

options.title: Approve the write-scoped handoff
options.body: Allow synthetic `operator.write` at this subagent-only chokepoint, retain explicit admin only for cleanup, and require live regression proof before merge.

options.title: Require delegated caller identity
options.body: Pause this patch and design an explicit delegated capability that preserves the originating principal through the internal RPC.

recommendation.title: Approve the write-scoped handoff
recommendation.body: Allow synthetic `operator.write` at this subagent-only chokepoint, retain explicit admin only for cleanup, and require live regression proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They co-developed and merged the original in-process dispatch behavior and are the strongest history-backed owner for the intended trust boundary.
